uncited: - **Voxel Grid:** A 3D array storing per-voxel attributes.
A voxel $i$ is pruned if its maximum weight over all training rays falls below a threshold.
**Repeat:** Continue optimizing at the new resolution.
**Define Known Free Space:** A query point is in known free space if the post-activated alpha value from $V^{(\text{density})(c)}$ is less than threshold $\tau^{(c)}$.
**Fine Voxels Allocation:** Densely query $V^{(\text{density})(c)}$ to find a BBox tightly enclosing the unknown space, with lengths $L_x^{(f)}, L_y^{(f)}, L_z^{(f)}$.
**Fine-stage Points Sampling:** Filter out rays not intersecting known free space.
Adjust near/far bounds $t^{(\text{near})}$ and $t^{(\text{far})}$ to ray-box intersection endpoints.
- A feature voxel grid $V^{(\text{feat})(f)} \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times N_x^{(f)} \times N_y^{(f)} \times N_z^{(f)}}$.
Inspired by NSVF, the voxel grids $V^{(\text{density})(f)}$ and $V^{(\text{feat})(f)}$ are progressively scaled.
Let $p_{g\_ckpt}$ be the set of checkpoint steps.
The initial number of voxels is set to $\lfloor M^{(f)} / 2^{|p_{g\_ckpt}|} \rfloor$.
When reaching a training step in $p_{g\_ckpt}$, the number of voxels is doubled such that the final number is $M^{(f)}$.
